sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test setup and reset
sections.what: Imports the test runner, the database, the seed function and the reset helper, and clears the database before the tests.
sections.why: Starts the seed test from an empty database.
sections.watch_out: The reset wipes the database it points at, so it must be a test database.

sections.name: seeding the committed fixtures (seed)
sections.title: Committed fixture seeding
sections.what: Runs the seed on the committed real fixtures and checks the cricket event count and that every sport produced incidents. Checks basketball is logged as not seeded. Runs the seed a second time and checks it adds no incidents or events. Checks no users were created.
sections.why: Likely reason: seeding must use real data only and must be safe to repeat.
sections.watch_out: The expected counts depend on the committed fixture files, so updating those files changes the results.

summary: Tests the database seeding step, which loads the committed real fixture data into the database and checks it is safe to run twice.
purpose: Makes sure the seed loads real match data, adds nothing on a second run, and creates no fake users.
why: Likely reason: seeding must use real recorded data only, and running it again must not create duplicates.
how: Resets the database, runs the seed with a log collector, checks the cricket event count and incident count, confirms each sport produced incidents and that basketball was skipped with a message, runs the seed again to confirm nothing new was added, and confirms no users exist.
inputs: Committed fixture files for cricket, football and F1, and the seeding function.
outputs: Pass or fail results and the seed log lines.
risks: The seed clears the test database through the reset helper, so it must never point at a real database. Expected counts depend on the committed fixtures.
debug: Read the seed log lines to see which sport failed. Check the fixture folder for missing files.
